# Keep Claude Code running when you close Paneflow

> Choose Keep sessions running when quitting, then reopen Paneflow to reconnect to Claude Code or Codex. The machine must stay awake.

Canonical: https://paneflow.dev/blog/keep-coding-agents-running

<!-- Auto-generated mirror of paneflow.dev - do not edit by hand.

     scripts/sync-public-docs.ts in the site repo. -->

Paneflow can keep Claude Code, Codex, and other terminal processes running after you close the app. Choose **Keep sessions running** when quitting, leave the machine awake, and reopen Paneflow to reconnect to the same live sessions.

## Close the app and return to your sessions

1. Save any files you edited in Paneflow and check whether an agent is waiting for an answer or permission.
2. Quit Paneflow and select **Keep sessions running** in the quit dialog. The app closes while the terminal processes remain active.
3. Reopen Paneflow on the same machine. It reconnects to the sessions that are still running. Read the latest output before sending your next instruction.

If the quit dialog no longer appears, check **When quitting with sessions running** in Settings. Select **Keep sessions running** to retain sessions automatically, or **Ask every time** to choose each time you quit.

## Why the terminals keep running

The Paneflow window displays the terminals, but a separate process, the **session host**, keeps them running. Quitting with **Keep sessions running** closes the interface and leaves that host active. An agent, development server, or long-running command can continue there while the app is closed.

Reopening Paneflow reconnects the interface to those processes. It does not need to relaunch the agent or load its conversation history. This behavior is documented in the [Paneflow 0.17.5 session persistence reference](https://github.com/arthjean/paneflow/blob/v0.17.5/docs/persistent-sessions.md).

## When you want to stop a session

To end one terminal session, select **Stop session** in its context menu in the sidebar. This ends its process. To end all terminal sessions as you quit, choose **Stop everything and quit**. Save any work you need before either action.

If Paneflow cannot confirm a stop, it keeps the window open and shows recovery choices for the affected sessions. Check their status before retrying: a timeout does not mean the process has stopped.

On the next launch after **Stop everything and quit**, Paneflow restores the layout with fresh shells. The previous agents are not relaunched. **Restart** on an ended terminal also starts a fresh shell without replaying its previous command. To load an agent's saved history, follow the [guide to resuming Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode conversations](/blog/agent-sessions).

## What to check before leaving

Keeping a process alive lets it continue working, but its progress still depends on the task and the machine:

- **Pending input or permission:** the agent keeps waiting until you respond. Paneflow does not approve requests for you.
- **Sleep:** execution can pause and network connections can drop. Leave the machine awake if you want work to continue.
- **Provider or network failure:** the process may remain alive while its task is interrupted. Check its output when you return.
- **Shutdown, reboot, or host crash:** the live process can end. Reopening the saved layout cannot restore it; resuming the conversation requires history saved by the agent.

The [terminal session documentation](/docs/features) explains the available reconnection and recovery controls.

## Check reconnection with a PowerShell counter

On Windows, you can check this behavior without starting an agent or making a model call. Open a PowerShell pane and run:

```powershell
Write-Output "PROCESS=$PID"
$tick = 0
while ($true) {
    Write-Output "TICK=$tick"
    $tick++
    Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
}
```

Note the process ID and counter value, then quit with **Keep sessions running**. Wait a few seconds and reopen Paneflow. The counter should have advanced without starting over at zero.

Press `Ctrl+C` to stop the loop, then run `Write-Output "PROCESS=$PID"` again. The same ID confirms that you reconnected to the original shell. `Ctrl+C` stops this counter while leaving the shell open.
